direction_as_read: Weakly positive: a pilot of ResistAid 4.5 g/day raised vaccine antibody response for 2 of 7 pneumococcal subtypes, with no effect on other immune markers
summary: Four labels print arabinogalactan 500 mg and one powder prints 2.4 g with other ingredients; two labels carry an immune purpose in the rows read. The one trial read, a Lonza-funded pilot of larch arabinogalactan ResistAid 4.5 g/day in 45 healthy adults, found a greater IgG response than placebo for 2 of 7 primary pneumococcal subtypes (20796315). The review of other trials isn't complete: the searches listed only the most recent hits, so older larch trials weren't seen.
question_for_clinician: 20796315 meets rule 2 for ResistAid at 4.5 g/day, with 2 of 7 primary antibody endpoints positive. Should these labels get credit, given they print arabinogalactan at 500 mg or 2.4 g with no brand or species, and the outcome is a surrogate from one sponsor-funded pilot? Agent recommendation: no credit in this review. Older larch trials weren't seen in the listed search hits and should be checked before a final ruling.

population.description: 45 healthy adults not previously vaccinated against Streptococcus pneumoniae.

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group pilot study, 72 days, with vaccination at day 30

outcomes.name: Pneumococcal IgG, 7 subtypes: greater response than placebo in 2 subtypes (18C, 23F) at days 51 and 72; the other 5 did not reach significance
Salivary IgA, white cell count, inflammatory cytokines and complement: no effect in the abstract

limitations: Pilot study; the authors say no power calculation could be performed.
Seven primary endpoints; the passages read don't name a correction for that.
Lonza supplied the product and gave financial support for all aspects of the study.
A vaccine antibody response is a surrogate; no infection outcome.
Dose is 4.5 g/day; four labels print 500 mg and one prints 2.4 g with other ingredients.
Abstract read; open full text read only in the passages on design, dose, funding and primary outcome.
Drafted from the source by agent review (Claude) on 2026-11-04; not clinician reviewed.

dose.reported_regimen: ResistAid 4.5 g powder mixed in a beverage once daily in the morning, or placebo, for 72 days.

normalization.basis: Assigned daily amount as printed in the source; no conversion.
